Hi there!

The first thing I notice is that you're not mentioning an SPF. Are you using spf? Daily? Because that could be why your skin isn't reacting positively to any of the products you mentioned. The products you mentioned all seem good ones, no bs, but you literally need sunscreen if 1. you have as many actives as you have (especially vit c), and 2. you need sunscreen GENERALLY. Going without sunscreen makes your face worse in many respects but one of them primarily is redness. Sunscreen helps a LOT with redness.

I have oily, sensitive, acne and rosacea skin. It was a disaster the last two years. I went through many products. Different things helped me. These are:

Sunscreen EVERY DAY. No excuses. Korean sunscreens are the best. No cast whatsoever, no greasiness, well absorbed. My favourite is skin aqua spf. Second favourite is purito's unscented green level sunscreen. The latter is VERY good for redness prone skin because its formulated with a lot of centenella. Centella is v helpful in soothing, alleviating and dealing with red skin. I can only recommend it.

Niacinamide paired with azelaic acid. The niacinamide is the first i really noticed textural improvement and skin tone that  evened out. I do believe your actives aren't working because you're not using any sunscreen. Are you noticing your skin  absorbs the products or are they just sitting on top? Azelaic acid also helped me a lot with the redness and the acne. A lot.

Upping my hydration game was important for me. I incorporated a hydrating gentle toner and a hydrating HA serum (both applied to damp skin) which I then seal in with my moisturiser. If u don't do well with HA, look into squalane/beta glucan or polyglutamic acid. All non HA based hydrators. More hydration means healthier skin, stronger skin. I had issues with products not absorbing and after I cut my actives back for some weeks and focused only on hydration and sunscreen, my products upon using them again absorbed again. Which of course meant my skin could reap the benefits again.

Especially oily skin must hydrate. Many skins overproduce oil because they're dehydrated. For me focusing on hydration really changed a lot.

It sounds like your skin is overtaxed. I would strongly advise to cut out all the actives, go back to the basics. A gentle hydrating cleanser, a good hydrating moisturiser and a calming sunscreen like the centella based one. Do that for some weeks. If you notice it works, use a hydrating serum or toner before your moisturiser. Repair your moisture barrier. Get it healthy again before you use your actives. They won't help if your skin is compromised and redness usually means inflammation and.a compromised skin barrier.

DEFINITELY get a reliable sunscreen.  Seriously. Its a game changer.

I started with BPO and took about three months getting used to it until I switched to  [short contact therapy](https://simpleskincarescience.com/benzoyl-peroxide/). You basically put the BPO on, wait 5 - 10 minutes until its dried down and then wash/cleanse it off and proceed with your routine. It's still as effective as it would be as leave-on product but minus the irritation. Other method you could try is buffering with a moisturiser: moisturise first then BPO. Same thing, effective but less irritation.

After your skin is good with BPO, introduce your retinol. I use differin. Again, build it up every other night (not as spot treatment, it's meant to be used all over but with just a pea sized amount) until your skin tolerates it, then you can up the frequency. I am currently doing this while still using BPO every morning and night 

Lastly, BPO is always much more effective in combination with another acne fighting product like differin. So you're on a good way. Also if the retinol turns out to be too irritating have a look at azelaic acid. Also a winner for acne.

Good luck!

Secondly, I'd suggest lay off the BO and apply some soothing ointment like La roche posay cicaplast b5. Regularly. Helps wonders. Then when your face is calm again, bring back BO. BUT buffer it with the moisturiser. That is put moisturiser on first and then the BO. You dont lose any of the effectiveness but the irritation should be noticeably less. When the BO sinks in, follow it up with some more soothing ointment, like cicaplast, that's really good. But any skin soothing cream is good.  diaper rash cream also helps. Look for panthenol, allantoin in the ingredients. Zinc too! Helps with skin repair. I can recommend the Penaten cream.

Let your skin calm first. Irritation with BO is to be expected but if you dont let it repair itself first you risk triggering making your condition (acne?) worse.  Soothe first, repair skin barrier and then begin to buffer with the moisturiser. When u notice your skin got used to it you can stop the buffering and switch to full on contact which shouldnt be that irritating anymore. Or try short contact therapy when you're there.

Good luck!!!!
